nodes.label: Reverse-Lookup Glossary
nodes.rationale: Turns a vague description of a motion effect into the precise term so the user knows what to ask for. It names effects; it does not design or build them.

nodes.label: Project Vocabulary Page
nodes.rationale: The glossary is a curated snapshot of the project's /vocabulary page; the two should be kept in sync when either changes.

nodes.label: Easing
nodes.rationale: The rate at which an animation speeds up or slows down.

nodes.label: Spring Animations
nodes.rationale: Physics-based motion as an alternative to fixed-duration easing.

nodes.label: Animation Performance
nodes.rationale: What keeps motion smooth instead of stuttering.

nodes.label: Principles to Know
nodes.rationale: Concepts that guide when and how to animate.

nodes.label: Pop In
nodes.rationale: An element appears with a slight overshoot, like it bounces into place.

nodes.label: Bounce
nodes.rationale: A spring that overshoots and settles, adding playfulness.

nodes.label: Scale In
nodes.rationale: An element grows from smaller to full size as it appears, often paired with a fade.

nodes.label: Reveal
nodes.rationale: Content is uncovered gradually, often by animating a clip-path or mask.

nodes.label: Clip-path
nodes.rationale: Clipping an element to a shape, used for reveals, masks, and before/after sliders.

nodes.label: Mask
nodes.rationale: Hiding or revealing parts of an element with a shape or gradient. Like clip-path, but with soft, fadeable edges.

nodes.label: Shared Element Transition
nodes.rationale: An element travels and transforms from one position into another, like a thumbnail expanding into a card.

nodes.label: Layout Animation
nodes.rationale: When an element's size or position changes, it animates to the new spot instead of snapping.

nodes.label: Crossfade
nodes.rationale: One element fades out as another fades in, in the same spot.

nodes.label: Morph
nodes.rationale: One shape smoothly turns into another shape, for example Dynamic Island.

nodes.label: Origin-Aware Animation
nodes.rationale: An element animates out of its trigger, like a popover growing from the button that opened it, instead of from its own center, which is the CSS default.

nodes.label: Transform Origin
nodes.rationale: The anchor point a scale or rotation grows or spins from.

nodes.label: Rubber-banding
nodes.rationale: Resistance and snap-back when you drag past a boundary, the iOS overscroll feel.

nodes.label: Spring
nodes.rationale: Motion driven by physics (tension, mass, damping) rather than a set duration.

nodes.label: Stiffness / Tension
nodes.rationale: How strongly the spring pulls toward its target. Higher feels snappier.

nodes.label: Damping
nodes.rationale: How quickly a spring settles. Lower damping means more bounce and oscillation.

nodes.label: Mass
nodes.rationale: How heavy the animated element feels. More mass makes it slower and more sluggish.

nodes.label: Momentum
nodes.rationale: Motion that carries velocity, especially after a drag or interruption.

nodes.label: Velocity
nodes.rationale: How fast and in which direction an element is moving. A spring carries it into the next animation when interrupted.

nodes.label: Interruptible Animation
nodes.rationale: An animation that can be smoothly redirected mid-flight instead of finishing first.

nodes.label: Perceptual Duration
nodes.rationale: How long a spring feels finished, even though it keeps micro-settling underneath.

nodes.label: Stagger
nodes.rationale: Animate several items one after another with a small delay between each, creating a cascade.

nodes.label: Ease-out
nodes.rationale: Starts fast, ends slow. The default for most UI and anything responding to the user.

nodes.label: Ease-in
nodes.rationale: Starts slow, ends fast. Usually avoided because it can feel sluggish.

nodes.label: Ease-in-out
nodes.rationale: Slow, fast, slow. Good for elements already on screen moving from A to B.

nodes.label: Linear Easing
nodes.rationale: Constant speed. Avoid for UI; reserve for spinners or marquees.

nodes.label: Cubic-bezier
nodes.rationale: A custom easing curve defined for precise control.

nodes.label: Keyframes
nodes.rationale: Defined points in an animation that the browser fills the gaps between.

nodes.label: Spatial Consistency
nodes.rationale: Animate so an element keeps its identity and position across states, so users never lose track of where things went.

nodes.label: Purposeful Animation
nodes.rationale: Motion should serve a function — orient, give feedback, or show relationships — not just decorate.

nodes.label: Frequency of Use
nodes.rationale: The more often a user sees an animation, the shorter and subtler it should be.

nodes.label: Perceived Performance
nodes.rationale: The right animation makes an interface feel faster, even when it is not.

nodes.label: Reduced Motion
nodes.rationale: Respect the user's prefers-reduced-motion setting by toning down or removing motion.

nodes.label: Hardware Acceleration
nodes.rationale: Animating transform and opacity lets the GPU keep motion smooth.

nodes.label: Layout Thrashing
nodes.rationale: Animating width, height, top, or left forces layout recalculation every frame and causes jank.

nodes.label: Compositing
nodes.rationale: Letting the GPU move or fade an element on its own layer without redoing layout or paint.

nodes.label: will-change
nodes.rationale: A CSS hint that an element is about to animate, so the browser can promote it to its own layer ahead of time.

nodes.label: Jank
nodes.rationale: Visible stutter when the browser drops frames because it cannot keep up with the animation.

nodes.label: Press / Tap Feedback
nodes.rationale: A subtle scale-down when an element is clicked, so it feels physical.

nodes.label: Swipe to Dismiss
nodes.rationale: Dragging an element off-screen to close it, like a drawer or toast.

nodes.label: Drag
nodes.rationale: Moving an element by grabbing it, often with momentum when released.

nodes.label: Parallax
nodes.rationale: Background and foreground move at different speeds while scrolling, creating depth.

nodes.label: Hold to Confirm
nodes.rationale: A progress effect that fills up while the user holds a button.

nodes.label: Blur
nodes.rationale: A blur filter used to soften an element or mask tiny imperfections.

nodes.label: Anticipation
nodes.rationale: A small wind-up in the opposite direction before a move, hinting at what is about to happen.

nodes.label: Follow-through
nodes.rationale: Parts of an element keep moving and settle slightly after the main motion stops, adding weight.

nodes.label: Squash and Stretch
nodes.rationale: Deforming an element as it moves to convey weight, speed, and flexibility.

nodes.label: Fluid Interface
nodes.rationale: An interface feels alive when motion starts from the current on-screen value, inherits the user's velocity, projects momentum forward, and can be grabbed and reversed at any instant. Springs make this natural because they are interruptible and velocity-aware.

nodes.label: Four Human Needs
nodes.rationale: Apple frames design as serving safety and predictability, understanding, achievement, and joy. Every motion rule serves one of them.

nodes.label: Response Latency
nodes.rationale: Respond on pointer-down, not on release, and keep feedback continuous during the gesture. The moment lag appears, the feeling of directness falls off a cliff.

nodes.label: Direct Manipulation
nodes.rationale: Touch and content should move together. Track 1:1 with Pointer Events and setPointerCapture, and respect the grab offset instead of snapping to the element center.

nodes.label: Interruptibility
nodes.rationale: Every animation must be redirectable at any moment from the live presentation value, never the logical target. CSS transitions and keyframes cannot be grabbed and reversed mid-flight, so gesture-driven motion should use springs. On reversal, blend velocity instead of hard-cutting it.

nodes.label: Springs Over Scripted Animation
nodes.rationale: A fixed-duration animation cannot respond to new input; a spring can, because new input only changes the target. Apple replaced mass, stiffness, and damping with damping ratio and response. Default damping is 1.0; damping near 0.8 is reserved for gestures that already carried momentum.

nodes.label: Damping Ratio
nodes.rationale: Controls overshoot. 1.0 is critically damped with no bounce. Below 1.0 overshoots and oscillates; lower is bouncier.

nodes.label: Spring Response
nodes.rationale: How quickly the value reaches the target, in seconds. This is not duration: a spring has no fixed duration, and its settle time emerges from the parameters.

nodes.label: Velocity Handoff
nodes.rationale: When a gesture ends, the animation must continue at the finger's exact velocity so there is no visible seam. Some spring APIs want relative velocity: gestureVelocity divided by remaining distance.

nodes.label: Momentum Projection
nodes.rationale: Do not snap from the release point. Project the resting position with exponential decay, (v/1000)*decelerationRate/(1-decelerationRate), then snap to the target nearest that projection. Apple does not ship the textbook v-squared over 2a form.

nodes.label: Spatial Consistency
nodes.rationale: If something disappears one way, it should emerge from where it came. Enter and exit along the same path, anchor popovers to their trigger with transform-origin, and mirror easing on reversible transitions.

nodes.label: Rubber-banding
nodes.rationale: At an edge, resist progressively instead of stopping hard. A hard stop reads as frozen; continuous resistance reads as responsive.

nodes.label: Gesture Feel Checklist
nodes.rationale: Highlight on touch-down and commit on touch-up. Require about 10px of hysteresis before locking a drag direction, recognize plausible gestures in parallel, and avoid recognizers that only report a final state.

nodes.label: Frame-Level Smoothness
nodes.rationale: Smoothness is about what is in the frames, not only the frame rate. Animate compositor-friendly transform and opacity, hint with will-change, and use requestAnimationFrame as the web equivalent of CADisplayLink.

nodes.label: Materials and Depth
nodes.rationale: Translucent materials convey hierarchy. On the web, approximate them with backdrop-filter. Never stack a light translucent surface on another, and materialize glass by animating blur with scale rather than fading opacity alone.

nodes.label: Multimodal Feedback
nodes.rationale: Motion, sound, and haptics must be causal, harmonious on the same frame, and useful. Reserve haptics and sound for meaningful moments so over-feedback does not train people to ignore it.

nodes.label: Reduced Motion and Accessibility
nodes.rationale: Reduced motion means a gentler, non-vestibular equivalent, not zero feedback. Replace slides, springs, and parallax with short opacity cross-fades, and also honor prefers-reduced-transparency and prefers-contrast as independent signals.

nodes.label: Optical Typography
nodes.rationale: Tracking and leading are size-specific. Large display text wants negative letter-spacing and tight leading; small text wants slightly positive tracking. Build hierarchy from weight, size, and leading together, and scale layout with the user's text size.

nodes.label: Eight Design Principles
nodes.rationale: Purpose, agency, responsibility, familiarity, flexibility, simplicity, craft, and delight. Delight is the result of the other seven, not decoration added on top.

nodes.label: Purpose
nodes.rationale: Make with intention and decide what not to build. Every feature spends the user's time, attention, and trust.

nodes.label: Agency
nodes.rationale: Keep people in control and back it with forgiveness. Confirm only genuinely destructive, irreversible actions.

nodes.label: Responsibility
nodes.rationale: Act in the user's interest: ask for privacy at the right moment, and anticipate misuse and harm, especially with AI.

nodes.label: Familiarity
nodes.rationale: Build on metaphors people already know and keep behavior consistent with appearance. Break a familiar pattern only when it is proven better.

nodes.label: Flexibility
nodes.rationale: Adapt to context, device, and the full range of abilities. When no single layout fits, let people personalize.

nodes.label: Simplicity
nodes.rationale: Strip the unnecessary so the core purpose shines. Simplicity is not minimalism: burying everything in one place looks minimal but is not simple.

nodes.label: Craft
nodes.rationale: Uncompromising, defensible detail builds trust. Jittery scroll, misaligned icons, and layouts that break on rotation read as carelessness.

nodes.label: Delight
nodes.rationale: Delight is the result of getting the other seven principles right, not confetti tacked on top. Decide the emotion and reinforce it in every decision.

nodes.label: Additive Animations
nodes.rationale: iOS carries velocity through a re-target so a reversal does not create a velocity discontinuity. On the web, choose a spring library that re-targets from the current velocity.

nodes.label: Pointer Capture
nodes.rationale: setPointerCapture keeps tracking even when the pointer leaves the element's bounds.

nodes.label: Designing Fluid Interfaces
nodes.rationale: WWDC 2018 talk that is the chief source for this fluid-motion model, including the momentum projection sample.

nodes.label: Designing Audio-Haptic Experiences
nodes.rationale: Source for the causality, harmony, and utility rules of combining motion, sound, and haptics.

nodes.label: The Details of UI Typography
nodes.rationale: WWDC 2020 talk on optical sizing, tracking, and leading.

nodes.label: Principles of Great Design
nodes.rationale: WWDC 2026 source for the eight design principles.

nodes.label: Motion / Framer Motion
nodes.rationale: Web spring libraries Apple's damping and response map onto. The bounce and duration spring API is the house-style mapping.

nodes.label: Vaul
nodes.rationale: Cited as a bottom-sheet that uses Apple-style momentum projection.

nodes.label: Embla
nodes.rationale: Cited as a carousel that uses Apple-style momentum projection.

nodes.label: Emil Kowalski
nodes.rationale: Author of the design-engineering philosophy encoded here and taught at animations.dev.

nodes.label: animations.dev
nodes.rationale: Emil Kowalski's course, cited as the deeper source for this philosophy.

nodes.label: Taste Is Trained
nodes.rationale: Good taste is a trained instinct built by studying why the best interfaces feel the way they do, not a personal preference.

nodes.label: Unseen Details Compound
nodes.rationale: Most details users never consciously notice. Their aggregate is what makes an interface feel right. Quoted from Paul Graham: unseen details sing in tune.

nodes.label: Beauty Is Leverage
nodes.rationale: People select tools on the overall experience. Good defaults and good animations are differentiators, and beauty is underused in software.

nodes.label: Before/After Review Table
nodes.rationale: UI reviews must be one markdown table with Before, After, and Why columns. A Before/After list is the wrong format.

nodes.label: Animation Decision Framework
nodes.rationale: Before writing animation code, answer in order: should it animate, what is the purpose, what easing, and how fast.

nodes.label: Frequency Gate
nodes.rationale: Never animate keyboard-initiated or 100-times-a-day actions; repetition makes motion feel slow and disconnected. Raycast ships no open/close animation for that reason. Tens per day should be reduced; occasional motion can be standard; rare moments can add delight.

nodes.label: Animation Purpose
nodes.rationale: Every animation must answer why it exists. Valid purposes are spatial consistency, state indication, explanation, feedback, and preventing jarring changes. Looking cool is not a purpose for something seen often.

nodes.label: Easing Decision
nodes.rationale: Entering or exiting uses a strong ease-out. On-screen movement uses ease-in-out. Hover and color use ease. Constant motion uses linear. Never use ease-in for UI: it delays the moment the user is watching, so the same duration feels slower.

nodes.label: UI Duration Budget
nodes.rationale: UI animations should stay under 300ms. Button feedback is 100-160ms, tooltips 125-200ms, dropdowns 150-250ms, modals and drawers 200-500ms. Faster motion feels more responsive even when the work takes the same time.

nodes.label: Perceived Performance
nodes.rationale: A fast spinner, a 180ms select, and instant subsequent tooltips make the app feel faster at the same actual speed. Ease-out feels faster than ease-in at the same duration because movement starts immediately.

nodes.label: Spring Animations
nodes.rationale: Springs have no fixed duration; they settle from physical parameters. Prefer Apple's duration-and-bounce API when reasoning about UI. Keep bounce in the 0.1-0.3 range and reserve it for drag-to-dismiss and playful motion. Springs keep velocity when interrupted, unlike keyframes.

nodes.label: Press Feedback
nodes.rationale: Buttons and other pressable elements use transform scale 0.97 on :active, with a 160ms ease-out. The scale should stay between 0.95 and 0.98.

nodes.label: Never Scale From Zero
nodes.rationale: Nothing in the real world appears from nothing. Start entrances from scale 0.95 or higher combined with opacity 0.

nodes.label: Origin-Aware Popovers
nodes.rationale: Popovers should scale from their trigger via the Radix or Base UI transform-origin variable. The default center origin is wrong for almost every popover.

nodes.label: Modal Origin Exception
nodes.rationale: Modals keep transform-origin center because they are not anchored to a trigger; they appear centered in the viewport.

nodes.label: CSS Transitions Over Keyframes
nodes.rationale: CSS transitions can be interrupted and retargeted mid-animation. Keyframes restart from zero. Use transitions for toasts, toggles, and anything triggered rapidly.

nodes.label: Blur Masks Crossfades
nodes.rationale: When a crossfade still shows two overlapping objects, a blur of about 2px blends them into one perceived transformation. Keep blur under 20px because heavy blur is expensive, especially in Safari.

nodes.label: @starting-style
nodes.rationale: The modern CSS way to animate entry without JavaScript. Fall back to a data-mounted attribute set from useEffect when browser support is missing.

nodes.label: GPU-Only Properties
nodes.rationale: Only animate transform and opacity so the work skips layout and paint. Do not drive a child transform by changing a CSS variable on the parent; that recalculates styles for every child.

nodes.label: Framer Motion Shorthand Caveat
nodes.rationale: Framer Motion x, y, and scale shorthands are not hardware-accelerated; they run on requestAnimationFrame and drop frames under load. Use a full transform string, or CSS, when the main thread is busy.

nodes.label: Web Animations API
nodes.rationale: JavaScript control with CSS performance: hardware-accelerated, interruptible, and no library required.

nodes.label: prefers-reduced-motion
nodes.rationale: Reduced motion means fewer and gentler animations, not zero. Keep opacity and color transitions that aid comprehension, and remove movement and position animations.

nodes.label: Hover Gating
nodes.rationale: Gate hover motion behind @media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine). Touch devices fire hover on tap and cause false positives.

nodes.label: Sonner Principles
nodes.rationale: Loved components win on developer experience, strong defaults, memorable names, invisible edge cases, transitions rather than keyframes, and a documentation site people can touch.

nodes.label: Motion Cohesion
nodes.rationale: Match easing and duration to the component's personality. Sonner is slightly slower and uses ease rather than ease-out so the motion matches the toast, the page, and the name.

nodes.label: Asymmetric Enter/Exit Timing
nodes.rationale: Slow where the user is deciding and fast where the system responds. Hold-to-delete fills over 2s linear; release snaps back in 200ms ease-out.

nodes.label: Stagger
nodes.rationale: Cascade group entrances with 30-80ms between items. Stagger is decorative and must never block interaction.

nodes.label: Momentum-Based Dismissal
nodes.rationale: Do not require dragging past a distance threshold. If velocity, distance over elapsed time, exceeds about 0.11, dismiss anyway. A flick should be enough.

nodes.label: Boundary Damping
nodes.rationale: Past a natural edge the element should move less the further it is dragged. Real things slow down before they stop; friction is better than an invisible wall.

nodes.label: Hold to Delete
nodes.rationale: A clip-path inset overlay fills over 2s linear while pressed and snaps back in 200ms ease-out on release, with scale 0.97 press feedback.

nodes.label: clip-path Animation
nodes.rationale: clip-path inset is an animation tool: scroll reveals, hold-to-delete overlays, seamless tab color wipes, and comparison sliders.

nodes.label: Percentage Translate
nodes.rationale: translate percentages are relative to the element itself. translateY(100%) moves by the element's own height, which is how Sonner and Vaul position toasts and drawers.

nodes.label: Sonner
nodes.rationale: Toast library whose defaults, naming, and cohesion are the worked example for these component principles.

nodes.label: Raycast
nodes.rationale: Cited as the correct case of no open/close animation, because the command palette is used hundreds of times a day.

nodes.label: Radix UI
nodes.rationale: Provides --radix-popover-content-transform-origin so popovers scale from their trigger.

nodes.label: Base UI
nodes.rationale: Provides --transform-origin so popovers scale from their trigger.

nodes.label: Vaul
nodes.rationale: Drawer library cited for translateY(100%) hiding and for gesture interaction.

nodes.label: Ionic Framework
nodes.rationale: Source of the iOS-like drawer curve cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1).

nodes.label: easing.dev
nodes.rationale: Recommended source for strong custom easings instead of hand-rolling curves.

nodes.label: easings.co
nodes.rationale: Recommended source for strong custom easings instead of hand-rolling curves.

nodes.label: Framer Motion
nodes.rationale: Motion, formerly Framer Motion. useSpring interpolates decorative mouse tracking; x/y/scale shorthands are not hardware-accelerated.

nodes.label: Dynamic Island
nodes.rationale: Cited as the kind of element that should feel alive and therefore use a spring.

nodes.label: Default to Flagging
nodes.rationale: A transition that merely runs but feels sluggish, lands from the wrong origin, fires too often, or drops frames is a regression. Approval is earned, not assumed.

nodes.label: Ten Non-Negotiable Standards
nodes.rationale: Every animation in a diff is measured against justified motion, frequency, easing, sub-300ms duration, origin and physicality, interruptibility, GPU-only properties, accessibility, asymmetric timing, and cohesion. A violation is a finding.

nodes.label: Justified Motion
nodes.rationale: Every animation must answer why it exists. Looking cool on a frequently seen element is a block.

nodes.label: Frequency-Appropriate Motion
nodes.rationale: Keyboard-initiated and 100-times-a-day actions get no animation. Tens per day are reduced. Occasional motion is standard. Rare moments may add delight.

nodes.label: Responsive Easing
nodes.rationale: Entering and exiting elements use ease-out or a strong custom cubic-bezier. ease-in on UI is a block because it delays the moment the user watches most.

nodes.label: Sub-300ms UI
nodes.rationale: UI animations stay under 300ms. Anything slower on a UI element needs justification. Per-element budgets live in the standards reference.

nodes.label: Origin and Physical Correctness
nodes.rationale: Popovers, dropdowns, and tooltips scale from their trigger. Never animate from scale(0); start from scale 0.9-0.97 plus opacity. Modals stay centered.

nodes.label: Interruptibility
nodes.rationale: Rapidly triggered or gesture-driven motion must retarget from the current state via CSS transitions or springs, not keyframes that restart from zero.

nodes.label: GPU-Only Properties
nodes.rationale: Animate transform and opacity only. Layout properties, or Framer Motion x/y/scale shorthands under load, are a performance finding.

nodes.label: Animation Accessibility
nodes.rationale: Honor prefers-reduced-motion with gentler motion, not zero: keep opacity and color, drop movement. Gate hover animations behind a fine-pointer hover query.

nodes.label: Asymmetric Enter/Exit
nodes.rationale: Deliberate actions animate slower; system responses snap. Symmetric timing on a press-and-release or hold is a finding.

nodes.label: Cohesion
nodes.rationale: Motion matches the component's personality and the rest of the product. When unsure whether motion feels right, the strongest move is often to delete it.

nodes.label: Aggressive Escalation Triggers
nodes.rationale: Flag on sight: transition all, scale(0), ease-in, keyboard animation, UI over 300ms, centered origin on a trigger-anchored popover, keyframes on rapid UI, layout properties, Framer shorthands under load, parent CSS variables driving child transforms, missing reduced-motion, ungated hover, symmetric press timing, and everything-at-once entrances.

nodes.label: Remedial Preference Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Prefer earlier fixes: delete the animation, reduce it, fix easing, fix origin, make it interruptible, move it to the GPU, make timing asymmetric, then polish, then accessibility and cohesion.

nodes.label: Findings Table
nodes.rationale: Required review output is one markdown table with Before, After, and Why. One row per issue. Never a Before/After list.

nodes.label: Verdict Tiers
nodes.rationale: Group remaining commentary by impact: feel-breaking regressions, missed simplifications, performance, interruptibility and timing, origin and cohesion, then accessibility.

nodes.label: Block Decision
nodes.rationale: Block on any feel-breaking regression, animation on a keyboard or high-frequency action, scale(0) or ease-in on UI, or a non-GPU animation with an easy GPU fix.

nodes.label: Approve Decision
nodes.rationale: Approve only when there is no feel-breaking regression, no obvious motion that should be deleted, durations and easing are in bounds, interruptibility is handled where needed, and reduced motion is respected.

nodes.label: Predetermined vs Gesture Motion
nodes.rationale: Prefer CSS transitions, @starting-style, or WAAPI for predetermined motion. Use JS and springs for dynamic, interruptible, gesture-driven motion.

nodes.label: Animation Standards Reference
nodes.rationale: Precise curves, durations, and rules to cite in review findings instead of approximating. Distilled from Emil Kowalski's design engineering philosophy.

nodes.label: Standard Easing Curves
nodes.rationale: Strong custom curves: ease-out cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1), ease-in-out cubic-bezier(0.77, 0, 0.175, 1), and the Ionic drawer curve cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1).

nodes.label: Duration Budgets
nodes.rationale: Button feedback 100-160ms, tooltips 125-200ms, dropdowns 150-250ms, modals and drawers 200-500ms. UI animations stay under 300ms.

nodes.label: Spring Configs
nodes.rationale: Apple-style spring is duration 0.5 and bounce 0.2. Traditional physics is mass 1, stiffness 100, damping 10. Bounce stays in 0.1-0.3 and is reserved for drag-to-dismiss and playful motion.

nodes.label: SVG Icon Sprite
nodes.rationale: A single SVG sprite that defines six symbol icons and does not instantiate them with use.

nodes.label: Bluesky Icon
nodes.rationale: Filled butterfly mark, viewBox 0 0 16 17, clipped by bluesky-clip.

nodes.label: Discord Icon
nodes.rationale: Filled Discord mark, viewBox 0 0 20 19, drawn as one path.

nodes.label: Documentation Icon
nodes.rationale: Three open strokes, viewBox 0 0 21 20: a page, a folded corner, and a pair of angle brackets.

nodes.label: GitHub Icon
nodes.rationale: Filled Octocat silhouette, viewBox 0 0 19 19, with fill-rule and clip-rule evenodd.

nodes.label: Social Icon
nodes.rationale: Two open strokes, viewBox 0 0 20 20: a person bust and a star badge.

nodes.label: X Icon
nodes.rationale: Filled X wordmark, viewBox 0 0 19 19, with fill-rule and clip-rule evenodd.

nodes.label: Two Icon Languages
nodes.rationale: Brand marks are solid #08060d fills. Documentation and social are unfilled #aa3bff strokes at width 1.35 with round caps and round joins.

nodes.label: Document With Code Chevrons
nodes.rationale: The page outline, folded corner, and opposing angle brackets make the documentation symbol read as a doc that contains code.

nodes.label: Person With Star Badge
nodes.rationale: A circular head, shoulder arc, and star make the social symbol read as a person marked as featured.

nodes.label: Hero Isometric Mark
nodes.rationale: Decorative brand illustration of two rounded-square plates in isometric view: a hollow white outline floating above a purple light-filled base, joined by dashed corner guides so the pair reads as one stacked object.

nodes.label: Layered Isometric Depth
nodes.rationale: The vertical gap, matching rounded-square footprints, and corner guides are the device that turns two separate plates into a single depth cue.

nodes.label: TypeScript Logo
nodes.rationale: 32 by 32 SVG on a 256-unit viewBox: a full-bleed square filled #007ACC, with a second white path drawing a T and an S.

nodes.label: Blue Square Field
nodes.rationale: First path, fill #007ACC, traces M0 128 v128 h256 V0 H0 and closes, covering the entire 256 viewBox.

nodes.label: Letter T
nodes.rationale: First subpath of the white path: a horizontal top bar near y=128 and a vertical stem about 94.68 units tall, closed with Z.

nodes.label: Letter S
nodes.rationale: Second subpath of the white path, begun by a relative move to the right of the T and built from cubic curves that form the S.

nodes.label: White Monogram Fill
nodes.rationale: Second path uses fill #FFF for both letter subpaths.

nodes.label: 32px Icon Viewport
nodes.rationale: width and height are 32 while viewBox is 0 0 256 256, so the artboard scales down to a small icon.

nodes.label: Decorative Brand Chip
nodes.rationale: aria-hidden="true" keeps the mark out of the accessibility tree, so the blue square and white TS read as a silent brand chip rather than as text.

nodes.label: Vite Logo
nodes.rationale: Accessible SVG titled Vite: a purple lightning bolt whose interior is a masked field of blurred purple, lavender, and cyan ellipses, flanked by parentheses that turn white in dark mode.

nodes.label: Lightning Bolt
nodes.rationale: Filled path using #9135ff that draws the Vite bolt silhouette.

nodes.label: Bolt Alpha Mask
nodes.rationale: Mask id a uses mask-type alpha and a bolt-shaped path so later paint is clipped to the mark.

nodes.label: Glow Ellipses
nodes.rationale: Rotated ellipses inside the masked group, filled #eee6ff, #8900ff, and #00c2ff.

nodes.label: Gaussian Foreground Blur
nodes.rationale: Filters b through p each run feFlood, feBlend, and feGaussianBlur at stdDeviation 7.659 or 4.596.

nodes.label: Bolt Color Palette
nodes.rationale: Bolt body #9135ff, purple streaks #8900ff, highlights #eee6ff, cyan accents #00c2ff.

nodes.label: Parenthesis Frame
nodes.rationale: A single path with class parenthesis draws a left and right parenthesis spanning the 47-unit height.

nodes.label: Dark Mode Parenthesis Fill
nodes.rationale: The parenthesis class is black by default and white under prefers-color-scheme dark so the frame stays visible on either background.

nodes.label: Mask-Clipped Interior Glow
